itinerary.summary: The City Palace, then a sunset boat to Jag Mandir.

place.name: City Palace
place.description: A cascade of palaces built over four centuries, with the Mor Chowk peacock mosaics and the mirrored Sheesh Mahal. The terraces frame Lake Pichola and the Lake Palace hotel below.

morning.tip: Rent the audio guide; the palace is a maze and the stories are the point.

place.name: Lunch at Ambrai Ghat
place.description: Cross to the quieter west bank for a lakeside lunch looking back at the City Palace, the classic Udaipur view.

afternoon.tip: Ask for a table on the ghat edge; it's the same view as the postcards.

place.name: Sunset boat to Jag Mandir
place.description: The palace boat ride stops at Jag Mandir, the island palace said to have inspired the Taj Mahal, and times the return for sunset.

evening.tip: Book the last sunset departure at the City Palace jetty in the morning; it sells out.

itinerary.theme: Old city and a royal sunset
itinerary.summary: Lanes, havelis, a folk show, and the hilltop Monsoon Palace.

place.name: Jagdish Temple and old-city lanes
place.description: A carved 17th-century Vishnu temple at the heart of the old city, then the lanes around it full of miniature-painting studios and silver shops.

morning.tip: Many studios run short painting demos; a good way to buy a genuine miniature.

place.name: Saheliyon ki Bari
place.description: The 'garden of the maidens', with marble elephants, lotus pools and fountains fed by gravity from Fateh Sagar Lake.

afternoon.tip: Pair it with a walk along Fateh Sagar's promenade afterwards.

place.name: Sajjangarh Monsoon Palace
place.description: A white hilltop palace above the city, built to watch monsoon clouds. At sunset you see every lake in Udaipur at once.

evening.tip: Vehicles go up from the sanctuary gate; the last one usually leaves around sunset, so don't linger past it.

itinerary.summary: A morning in the hills and a farewell dinner on the lake.

place.name: Eklingji and Nagda temples
place.description: Twenty kilometres north, Eklingji is the Mewar rulers' family temple, still in worship. Nearby Nagda's 10th-century Sas-Bahu temples sit quietly by a lake.

morning.tip: No phones or cameras inside Eklingji; leave them in the car.

place.name: Bagore ki Haveli
place.description: An 18th-century minister's mansion turned museum, with rooms of puppets, costumes and the world's 'largest turban'.

afternoon.tip: Come back at 7 PM for the Dharohar folk dance show in the courtyard (tickets at the gate).

place.name: Candlelit dinner facing the Lake Palace
place.description: End with dinner on a lakeside terrace looking at the illuminated Lake Palace, a fitting last night.

evening.tip: Reserve a lake-edge table a day ahead for a weekend night.

itinerary.dayTip: Most sights close by 6 PM; keep evenings for the lake.

stays.name: Taj Lake Palace
stays.why: The floating marble palace itself, reached only by boat; the ultimate couples' splurge.

stays.name: Jagat Niwas Palace
stays.why: Lake-view havelis with jharokha windows in the heart of the old city.

stays.name: Amet Haveli
stays.why: Quiet west-bank rooms facing the City Palace across the water.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Hindi and Mewari; English widely understood
essentials.weather: Oct-Mar is mild (10-28°C). Lakes are fullest after the Jul-Sep monsoon.
essentials.gettingAround: Autos for the old city; book a cab for Sajjangarh and Eklingji.
essentials.phrase: Padharo mhare des: welcome to my land

packing: Light jacket for winter evenings on the water

summary.overview: Udaipur for two: lake palaces, a sunset boat on Lake Pichola, old-city lanes and a day trip into the Aravalli hills, with candlelit dinners on the water.
highlights: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
The City Palace's mirror and peacock halls
